claim_checks.claim: Artifact: descriptors in Node 24 (the code block: literal property all flags true; defineProperty-created property all false; Math.PI all false)
claim_checks.page_says: not checked: cites only the local lab [^1], which has no saved text

claim_checks.claim: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(obj, key) returns the descriptor; Object.defineProperty(obj, key, descriptor) creates or updates one, and omitted flags default to false when creating
claim_checks.page_says: If the property exists, defineProperty updates its flags. Otherwise, it creates the property … if a flag is not supplied, it is assumed false.
claim_checks.note: [^2] also says getOwnPropertyDescriptor returns a descriptor holding the value and all the flags.

claim_checks.claim: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors plus Object.defineProperties clone an object with its flags and symbols
claim_checks.page_says: Together with Object.defineProperties it can be used as a “flags-aware” way of cloning an object … returns all property descriptors including symbolic and non-enumerable ones.

claim_checks.claim: writable: false. Assignment throws TypeError in strict mode and is silently ignored otherwise
claim_checks.page_says: In non-strict mode, no errors occur when writing to non-writable properties and such. But the operation still won’t succeed.
claim_checks.note: [^2] backs the error in strict mode and the silent failure otherwise, but its error line ('Error: Cannot assign to read only property') never names TypeError (searched 'TypeError'). The error class rests only on the local lab [^1], so the claim as a whole cannot be grounded here. [^4] names TypeError for frozen objects in strict mode but is not cited.

claim_checks.claim: enumerable: false. The property is skipped by for…in, Object.keys and JSON.stringify, but direct access still works
claim_checks.page_says: Then it won’t appear in a for..in loop, just like the built-in one … Non-enumerable properties are also excluded from Object.keys
claim_checks.note: [^2] backs for…in and Object.keys. JSON.stringify skipping and direct access still working: not found in [^2] (searched 'JSON', 'stringify', 'direct'); those parts rest only on the local lab [^1].

claim_checks.claim: configurable: false. The property cannot be deleted, and its flags cannot be changed — except that writable can still go from true to false
claim_checks.page_says: A non-configurable property can’t be deleted, its attributes can’t be modified. … We can change writable: true to false for a non-configurable property

claim_checks.claim: Both a redefinition and a delete threw TypeError in strict mode
claim_checks.page_says: not checked: cites only the local lab [^1], which has no saved text

claim_checks.claim: preventExtensions forbids new properties; seal also makes all properties non-configurable; freeze also makes them non-writable
claim_checks.page_says: Forbids the addition of new properties to the object. … Sets configurable: false for all existing properties. … Sets configurable: false, writable: false for all existing properties.
claim_checks.note: Each helper also forbids adding properties, so 'all properties' and 'all existing properties' are the same set. [^4] confirms freeze prevents extensions and makes existing properties non-writable and non-configurable.

claim_checks.claim: They are shallow: a frozen object's nested object stays mutable
claim_checks.page_says: not checked: cites only the local lab [^1], which has no saved text
claim_checks.note: [^4] says this ('freeze is shallow') and the References entry says [^4] backs shallowness, but this sentence does not cite it.

claim_checks.claim: Accessors. get full() {…} runs on read, set full(v) {…} on assignment; the descriptor has get/set and no value/writable
claim_checks.page_says: The getter works when obj.propName is read, the setter – when it is assigned. … there is no value or writable, but instead there are get and set functions.

claim_checks.claim: A descriptor with both get and value is invalid (TypeError)
claim_checks.page_says: If we try to supply both get and value in the same descriptor, there will be an error: // Error: Invalid property descriptor.
claim_checks.note: [^3] backs 'invalid, throws an error' but does not name TypeError (searched 'TypeError'); the error class rests only on the local lab [^1].

claim_checks.claim: Smart getters for compatibility. An accessor can keep an old property name working while the data moves — e.g. derive age from a stored birthday
claim_checks.page_says: Instead of age we may decide to store birthday, because it’s more precise and convenient … Adding a getter for age solves the problem
not checked: cites only the local lab [^1], which has no saved text

conflicts.topic: Do flag-violating operations throw only in strict mode? [^2]: 'Errors appear only in strict mode … silently ignored in non-strict'. [^4]: attempts fail 'silently or by throwing a TypeError exception (most commonly, but not exclusively, when in strict mode)', with non-strict examples where Object.defineProperty on a frozen object and push on a frozen array throw TypeError.
conflicts.winner: none: [^2] rank 3 and [^4] rank 3 are the same rank and no Rank 1 source is cached to settle it
conflicts.loser: [^2] rank 3 (as a general rule; both sources agree for plain assignment)
conflicts.where_loser_is: ## Trade-offs (Object.freeze row: 'strict-mode-only errors', uncited and not marked ⚠️); ## Edge cases row 3 Why cell ('Errors only in strict mode')

conflicts.topic: Does freeze set writable: false on all existing properties ([^2]) or only on data properties ([^4])?
conflicts.winner: no real conflict: accessor properties have no writable attribute ([^3]), so both describe the same effect

violations.evidence: C19: the row names TypeError for assigning to a getter-only property; [^3] says only 'there will be an error' and '// Error (property has only a getter)'.

The Object.freeze row states 'strict-mode-only errors' as fact. Same-rank cited sources disagree: [^2] says errors appear only in strict mode, while [^4] says freeze violations throw TypeError 'most commonly, but not exclusively, when in strict mode' and shows Object.defineProperty and push on a frozen object throwing outside strict mode. The difference is not marked ⚠️ or attributed; the Why cell of ## Edge cases row 3 repeats the general rule.

No section holds role 2 (parts) or role 5 (reference values) of its own: the flag defaults and per-helper effects are spread across ## Mental model and the steps of ## How it works, which mixes mechanism with reference rules. ## Takeaways repeats the false-defaults point already made in ## How it works step 1 and ## Trade-offs.
